text:
alex: FYI spotted a big latency spike on shared-gpu-pool-7 around 15:12 UTC, looks correlated with tenant bursts. open to hypotheses.

maria: saw that too. p50 stayed ok but p99 jumped to ~820ms for text-gen. Any recent kernel changes? :thinking_face:

sam: nothing deployed to runtime today that should affect kernel selection. but we did push a batching heuristic tweak yesterday. could be interaction.

infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: pool-shared-7 p99_lat > 600ms for 3m (source=latency-monitor)

jess: sharing traces — when I sampled traces, a bunch of requests used the fp16-vecmul kernel instead of the fused-attn for seq_len ~512. suspicious.

alex: that matches my flamegraphs. heavy tenant (tenant-a) was sending lots of mid-length requests which triggered a different kernel choice, and that forced kv cache misses on other tenants.

kai: can you paste the kernel selection log snippet?

jess: here: ```[2026-02-18T15:12:05Z] model=redwood-large seq=512 batch=8 selected_kernel=matmul_fp16 fallback=fused_attn reason="est_cost_lower"```

maria: interesting — estimator thought matmul_fp16 cheaper at that batch/seq, but matmul path increases memory movement and evicts per-tenant KV lanes. so cross-tenant eviction -> recompute -> higher tail latency.

sam: profiling capture: ```KVCache: evictions=2384, avg_fetch_ms=12.6, reloads=2140; GPU_util=92%``` that many reloads will spike token latency.

alex: so root chain: tenant-a burst -> scheduler batches combine seq lengths -> kernel selector chooses matmul_fp16 -> KV cache pressure -> eviction and reloads for tenant-b/c -> p99 spike.

oncall: can we throttle tenant-a or apply per-tenant batch caps temporarily?

maria: we have per-tenant limits but they were set loose to favor throughput. suggest emergency mitigation: set per-tenant concurrent_batches=2 for tenant-a on pool-7 and force kernel selector to favor fused_attn for seq>=384 for 1h.

sam: will roll a runtime flag to bias kernel selection (kc_bias=fused_attn) for pool-7, and add a KV cache soft-reserve per-tenant to lower cross-tenant evictions. rolling now.

infra-bot: Deploy started: runtime-config/pool-7/kc_bias -> fused_attn (id=deploy-8973)

jess: after bias applied, p99 dropped to 210ms within ~90s. KV evictions fell to ~120 in the last 5m.

alex: good. we should follow up with a non-emergency plan: 1) refine kernel cost model to account for KV cache churn, 2) add per-tenant KV soft-reserves, 3) make batching heuristics aware of mixed-length batches across tenants.

maria: agreed. Also add a regression test: simulate tenant mix and verify p99 under stress. put it in eng-runtime backlog with priority high.

sam: I'll open the ticket and attach the flamegraphs/profiles. tag me if you want to pair on the kernel cost model changes.

jess: thanks all. putting a short postmortem in /incidents and notify support to inform affected customers. :white_check_mark:
